scope_note: Only the mid_mid course is calibrated/verified against these values. The other 8 courses are unverified for this gear/contact-material combination (see envs/baseball_b1_env.py's CROSSING_TIME_S comment).

solver.refsafe_note: refsafe clamps any geom-level solref[0] (timeconst) below 2*timestep to that floor. The measured ball-bat effective timeconst below (0.0051s) is already 10x above the 0.0005s floor, so refsafe is NOT clamping it in this configuration -- included here only so a future timestep change can re-check this.

ground.note: inherited from <default>, unaffected by the ball_geom override

actual_measured_ball_bat_contact.measured_via: data.contact[i].solref / .solimp read directly during a real mid_mid collision (OracleAimController, seed=0), not derived analytically
actual_measured_ball_bat_contact.explanation: MuJoCo mixes two equal-priority, equal-solmix (1.0) geoms' contact params by SIMPLE ARITHMETIC MEAN, not by taking the softer/lower-priority geom's own value. solref: (0.0002+0.01)/2=0.0051 (matches). solimp[2]: (0.0001+0.001)/2=0.00055 (matches). This corrects an earlier (wrong) claim in this codebase's comments/VALIDATION_LOG that 'the pair uses the softer/lower-priority of the two geoms' and that ball_geom's own declared solref was the value actually governing the collision -- see https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/modeling.html#contact-parameters for MuJoCo's own documented mixing rule.

gear_calibration.method: Sweep bat_motor gear in {12,20,30,45,60} x a per-gear trigger-time search (center = isolated swing-alone time from prep_swing=-1.9 to the mid_mid alignment angle -1.298rad, +-0.04s window, 0.001-0.002s resolution), with the ball_geom solref override already applied. Selected the smallest gear giving a clearly positive exit velocity and forward_flight_success -- not the single fastest/highest bat-speed candidate (45/60 had higher raw contact-point speed but overshot the alignment angle too fast for the achievable trigger resolution to land a well-aligned hit).

candidates.note: also succeeds, gear=30 kept for more margin

tilt.note: 2.75x the naive rod-about-end geometric estimate (0.2168) -- used for the I-07b-followthrough brake gain derivation, docs/records/VALIDATION_LOG.md

central_case_final_verification.tilt_settle_status: not confirmed within the episode's natural lifetime (ball lands ~0.70s after latch); final in-episode state angle=-2.1e-4rad, vel=0.061rad/s (both well converged, no divergence/repeated reversal), see docs/records/VALIDATION_LOG.md for the full discussion of why tilt's gear=6 torque authority cannot meet the 0.5s design target against this disturbance magnitude

caveats: Reflects real, converged MuJoCo contact-solver behavior (verified dt-independent down to 5e-6s, 25x finer than production), not a claim of real bat-ball coefficient-of-restitution accuracy.

No independent energy/momentum/impulse cross-check against real baseball bat-ball physics was performed -- see docs/design/FOLLOWTHROUGH-AND-FLY-MODEL.md section B's explicit caution against tuning material purely to pass the 5m gate.
gear=30/ball_geom solref combination is verified for mid_mid only.
